title: select grammar in one class: find options, the three join kinds, clause order, and the in operator
instruction: In the sandbox model, create a class DemoCustomerQueries whose methods each exercise one part of the select grammar that the report cases never reach. Ground it first with get_knowledge(topic="select-statement"). All methods public static. (1) `container topGroups()` - reads at most ten rows with the firstOnly10 find option (not a loop counter). (2) `boolean hasCustomers(CustGroupId _group)` - uses an EXISTS JOIN, whose joined buffer fetches no fields and cannot be read in the body; a plain join plus a RecId test FAILS this case. (3) `container groupsWithoutCustomers()` - uses a NOTEXISTS JOIN. (4) `container groupNamesWithCounts()` - aggregates with count() and group by. The ordering clause belongs BEFORE the where of the same segment: `select ... order by X where Y` compiles, `select ... where Y order by X` is a compile error whose message is only "'join' expected". (5) `boolean blockedInAny(CustAccount _account, container _states)` - filters an ENUM field with the `in` operator. The right side must be a container VARIABLE: an inline literal answers "Container literals in 'in' expression are not supported. Declare container variable instead.", and a str or int64 field answers "Types 'str(...)' and 'container' are not compatible with operator 'in'". Confirm every field you read with get_object_info before writing it. Build with zero errors and zero BP errors.
